newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-MONTGOMERIE RECOVERS FORM WITH A 64.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-MONTGOMERIE RECOVERS FORM WITH A 64.

text.p: European number one Colin Montgomerie recovered from Sunday's disastrous 76 to shoot a week's-best eight-under-par 64 in the final round of the British PGA Championship at Wentworth on Monday.
But the big Scot was unhappy with his inconsistency and suggested he might have been thinking too much about technique during Sunday's round.
"For the past nine years my game has been based on being consistent, but 76-64 is not consistent so something is not quite right," he said.
"I would rather have played two 70s to go from six under to 10 under than do what I did."

Montgomerie, who shot 69 in his first two rounds, ended up in fifth place and took heart from his recovery ahead of this week's Tournament Players Championship in Hamburg and next month's U.S. Open at the Congressional course outside Washington.
"Sunday's round was very poor for someone of my calibre, so it's nice to get it back," the world number six said. "I was thinking last night what had gone wrong, I had a chat with myself.
"This year has never got off the ground. I've been stuttering my way through tournaments."
Montgomerie, top in Europe for four seasons, said the best way for him to play "is not to think about things and just play each shot as it comes. I have been doing that for nine years.

"I have become bogged down by technique. As a result I have been steering the ball. But (my caddy) Alistair and I worked out a couple of things last night and it's amazing the way things worked out today."

Montgomerie, who appeared to have recovered his form when he won the European zone of the Andersen Consulting world championship last Tuesday, said his 64 was the worst he could have shot, given how he played.
"I missed three eagle putts of 20 feet or less, plus I missed a short putt of six feet at the eighth and at the ninth I missed a 15-footer. So I had chances."
Montgomerie denied that playing on Sunday with Nick Faldo, who has an intimidating effect on some players, contributed to his poor performance.
"It was nothing to do with that. I enjoy playing with Nick and always have done.
"Perhaps I will play with him in the Ryder Cup," he said. "If I do, I hope I'll be a better partner than I would have been on Sunday."
